name: Strata Deep TunnelHide Mining Pressure Suit
description:
A hard-use tunneling and deep-mining suit designed for the pressurized subterranean extraction zones beneath M88. Outer shell is abrasion-resistant cordura-steel weave in matte charcoal, reinforced with ABS polymer impact panels at knees, elbows, and shoulders — panels are frequently cracked and field-replaced with scrap. A built-in exoframe harness runs along the spine and hips, providing load-bearing support for heavy equipment carry without a separate exoskeleton purchase.

The suit's hood integrates a sealed face shield with dust filtration and low-light optical enhancement. Collar carries a pressure equalization valve for rapid descent environments. Most miners mark their suits with paint or carved notches — personal identification in low-light tunnels where faces are hidden.
functionality: Impact and abrasion protection for tunnel environments. Spine-hip exoframe offloads up to 40kg of carried equipment weight. Pressure equalization valve rated for rapid descent to 400m. Low-light optical enhancement integrated into face shield. Spinal channel accommodates aug spinal rigs. Reinforced knee panels extend to digitigrade leg configurations.
what_it_says: You go underground and you come back up — you've made peace with the difference between those two things.
worn_by: Shelf tunnel-market operators who need protection
manufacturer: Strata Deep Industrial (Tier 2 corponation); knockoff panels from Shelf fabricators
story_hooks: A miner's suit has 47 carved notches on the left forearm — one for each shift at a depth that officially doesn't exist on any city map.
A tunnel collapse survivor was found three weeks later, suit still sealed — the pressure valve had kept them alive in a pocket, but the company had already filed the death paperwork.
Someone is running a side business selling 'certified' Strata Deep suits with forged inspection stamps; the exoframe harness bolts are the wrong alloy and will shear under load.
